assembly_notes: One guide_rail part owns the rail cross-section, the rail_mount structure and the end_treatment hardware; carriage_count bearing_carriage parts each get one +X prismatic joint whose origin is solved by mate_planes between the rail race plane and the carriage race footprint. rail_mount sets mount_top_z, rail_profile sets seat_z and the capture cavity, end_treatment sets end_margin, and carriage_block sets carriage_footprint_x -- all four feed the same travel/zone DAG, so every one of the 24 core combinations builds. Captured contact is made only by bearing-ball spheres biting 0.6 mm into the race; no allow_overlap is emitted anywhere and no joint is clamped.

derived.expression: mount_top_z + neck_height + 0.4*shaft_radius + shaft_radius  (round_shaft) | mount_top_z + base_thickness + crown_height  (profile_rail)
derived.name: seat_z
derived.rationale: the joint origin z comes from mate_planes on the active race plane, so the block height follows both the rail_mount height and the rail cross-section

derived.name: carriage_footprint_x
derived.rationale: the consumer footprint the seat must host, including end seals and any flange overhang

derived.name: usable_half
derived.rationale: provider extent along the rail; end_margin comes from the end_treatment candidate

derived.name: travel
derived.rationale: prismatic lower/upper = -travel/+travel; both limits are exercised by motion QC

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: carriage_length is clamped to zone_len - 0.004 - 2*0.010 - 2*seal_proud - flange_extra so every declared count keeps travel >= 0.010 m and a 4 mm gap between neighbours at facing extremes
multiplicities.name: carriage_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: usable span 2*usable_half is split into carriage_count equal zones; carriage i homes at zone centre home_x[i] = -usable_half + zone_len*(i+0.5) and its symmetric bound is travel = (zone_len - carriage_footprint_x - 0.004)/2

candidates.name: round_shaft
candidates.notes: Bore radius derives as shaft_radius + 1.2 mm so the housing never touches the shaft; capture comes from two bearing balls at the crest of the bore.
